provenance.prompt:
Generate a transparent pixel-art atlas with TWO square cells side-by-side, first FRONT end elevation, second REAR end elevation, for the exact gated sandstone footbridge shown in the attached four-panel geometry reference. It contains labeled canonical source, accepted TOP plan, accepted RIGHT long side, and accepted LEFT long side. Source fixes identity/colors; TOP and side views fix footprint and height.

Strict orthographic front/rear end-on views: camera horizontally level at bridge height, looking along the bridge length, no perspective, no isometric tilt, no view of the top deck surface. The bridge length runs away from this camera, so compress that length to a very thin edge. Match the accepted side-view parapet height exactly: total end-profile silhouette should be a LOW horizontal band, about 1/3 as tall as its width (roughly 2.8:1 width-to-height), not a tall façade. Max height of stonework and iron is about one third of total horizontal width.

Build just a shallow horizontal bridge-end silhouette: two compact square stone end piers, each only about one block high; a low dark iron gate/rail between them with a straight horizontal top beam and several short vertical bars; a very thin dark stone deck edge along the bottom. The gate and piers all stay within the same low parapet height visible from RIGHT/LEFT. FRONT is the approach gate, REAR is the opposite end with matching low stone piers/rail, not an upright arch. The top plan has three masonry sections running along bridge length; those are depthwise and MUST NOT become stacked vertical blocks in these views. Do not draw a large vertical gate, a full wall, tall towers, any three-course vertical piers, walkway top plane, or broad front façade. The endpoint has no raised tower structure.

Use pale sandstone blocks, charcoal seams, muted dark iron as in the source. Center the compact shallow band in the lower half of each cell with ample transparent margin. Keep full silhouette inside each cell. Crisp pixel clusters, no labels, shadows, stray guide marks, cross-cell artifacts.
provenance.notes: Root-scoped-accepted principal end elevation installed with current source and all-six hash guards. FRONT/REAR use v4 low gate end profiles (173x56); RIGHT/LEFT use v2 accepted long parapet profiles. TOP/BOTTOM retained.

provenance.prompt:
Create a transparent-background pixel-art atlas with exactly four side-by-side views of the same Early Arenas gated stone bridge, in order FRONT, RIGHT, LEFT, REAR. The attached native source and accepted TOP/BOTTOM define a narrow horizontal stone walkway running along world Y, with a barred black-metal gate across the FRONT/south end and matching short stone parapet/posts on both sides. Use the source as identity authority and accepted plan views for exact orientation. Do not use the hybrid top-down source as a camera angle.

Strict axis-aligned orthographic views, no isometric/perspective/foreshortening, fixed world orientation. FRONT looks from -Y toward the gate end: show one straight-on low gate elevation across the short width, barred gate centered between two stone end posts, stone walkway side edges receding only as very thin depth, no full top-down walkway rectangle. REAR looks from +Y at the opposite end: show the far stone cross-end/parapet and walkway edge, not the front gate bars repeated. RIGHT and LEFT look from +/-X at the long bridge sides: each must show one long horizontal stone parapet/sidewall running along Y, a low continuous walkway/beam edge and the correct repeated stone posts; the gate appears only as a small vertical end edge at the FRONT endpoint, never as the whole image. Right/left are long side elevations, not gate-end views and not narrow vertical posts.

Keep identical scale, height and materials across directions. Stone parapets and posts are gray-beige masonry; gate bars are dark iron only at the front end. No invented doors, extra rails, banners, or structures. Four isolated complete views, transparent margins, no labels, no shadows, crisp Pocket Dungeon pixel-art clusters.
provenance.notes: Root-scoped-accepted principal end elevation installed with current source and all-six hash guards. FRONT/REAR use v4 low gate end profiles (173x56); RIGHT/LEFT use v2 accepted long parapet profiles. TOP/BOTTOM retained.

provenance.prompt:
Create a crisp pixel-art atlas on a fully transparent background, exactly SIX COLUMNS by SIX ROWS, no text or borders. Columns in exact order FRONT, TOP, RIGHT, LEFT, BOTTOM, REAR. Rows in exact order faction-larracos-larracos-college-of-magic-entrance; iron-tracks-tunnel-stone-open-doorway; hunting-jungle-vine-covered-ruin-stone-open-doorway; industry-menagerie-soot-stained-brick-open-doorway; faction-battlefield-fortified-camp-gate; early-arenas-gated-stone-bridge. The attached contact sheet has a canonical SOURCE followed by current views in each row; the SOURCE is the authority for that row’s material, ornament, count, and open/closed state. Preserve source identity exactly; never borrow another row’s motifs. True orthographic axis-aligned views only, no isometric or perspective. FRONT/REAR are straight elevations with no visible top; TOP looks straight down and BOTTOM straight up; RIGHT/LEFT are edge-on side elevations. Keep consistent physical proportions across directions. Each cell contains one object, centered, separated with transparent margin; no detached specks or neighboring-cell overlap.

ROW 1 faction-larracos-larracos-college-of-magic-entrance: pale carved stone arch with blue magical inset and paired small statues. TOP must be the full shallow arch, pillar, statue-base footprint seen from directly above, with no frontal arch face; BOTTOM is the matching pale-stone foundation underside, same complete footprint, no generic square panel. Preserve paired statues; do not invent posts or extra objects.

ROW 2 iron-tracks-tunnel-stone-open-doorway: open stone tunnel portal with moss and dark passage. TOP is only the shallow lintel and post-cap surfaces in plan, with dark opening empty; BOTTOM is the matching threshold/foot underside, not a frontal wall with stacked masonry courses. Preserve visible opening and source moss/stone.

ROW 3 hunting-jungle-vine-covered-ruin-stone-open-doorway: open overgrown stone doorway with vines. TOP is a compact orthographic arch/frame footprint with thin vine and stone edge details, not a floor tile; BOTTOM is the matching stone foundation underside. REAR shows the reverse side of the same open through-passage: paired jambs and arch, empty opening, not a sealed masonry wall.

ROW 4 industry-menagerie-soot-stained-brick-open-doorway: open soot-dark brick and stone arch with steel corner braces. TOP is a shallow arch-lintel plan with cap stones above the passage, not an upright frontal arch; BOTTOM is a matching narrow foundation/threshold underside, not the front door face. REAR is the reverse elevation with the same open passage, no brick wall closing it. Keep the source dark red brick and gray stone.

ROW 5 faction-battlefield-fortified-camp-gate: rough timber gate with two posts, beam, hanging green cloth banners and rocks. TOP has the gate beam and two post caps/rocks as an overhead footprint; hanging cloth presents as thin hems, not broad flag faces. BOTTOM has timber post-foot undersides and ground-anchored structure at the same footprint, not a generic full square ground patch. Preserve the source two-post count and green cloth.

ROW 6 early-arenas-gated-stone-bridge: dark timber bridge deck between pale stone posts and railings. FRONT/REAR are bridge-end elevations with the deck edge and paired stone posts, not the overhead walkway tilted upright. RIGHT/LEFT are long low side elevations with horizontal bridge deck and railing spans along X, coherent with the source plan. Keep the same count of stone posts, no additional gates or panels.

provenance.prompt:
Create one isolated transparent-background pixel-art BOTTOM principal view, camera directly below looking straight up, of the same old Havana colonial arcade building in the canonical source. The attached labeled source and accepted FRONT/TOP/RIGHT/LEFT/REAR views are authoritative for building identity, actual footprint, material, and scale; ignore/reconstruct past the held old bottom view because it is a frontal balcony fragment.

BOTTOM must be a true underside projection of the complete building footprint, with the same broad XY outline/depth as the TOP plan. Show a coherent warm cream/ochre masonry foundation underside or timber support soffit matching the source construction, with compact support/piers visible only as cross-sections at their actual positions. The front balcony, arches, columns, windows and vertical facade must be occluded from below; do not show any upright facade, balcony rail, arch opening, column shaft, roof top, or frontal scene. No generic metal tray, bolts, or invented ornament. Preserve source-appropriate plaster/stone/timber materials and physically plausible supports. Straight orthographic projection, no perspective, no isometric tilt. Center full footprint with transparent margin and no clipping, labels, shadow, or detached guide pixels. Crisp pixel art.

provenance.prompt:
Create a transparent-background pixel-art atlas in the SAME Pocket Dungeon style, palette, outline weight, and cluster scale as the attached labeled source-plus-six contact sheet. It has exactly 6 columns in this order: FRONT, TOP, RIGHT, LEFT, BOTTOM, REAR; exactly 3 rows in this order: (1) great-race fractured-maze ground slab, (2) jungle bugbear timber shelter, (3) iron-stations platform edge segment. Every cell contains one complete isolated view of the same physical source object in that row, centered with generous transparent margins. Strict axis-aligned orthographic projection, camera aligned exactly to world axes, no isometric/perspective/foreshortening, no rotation of the object between views, no shadows or labels, no neighboring-cell bleed.

For all rows, FRONT and REAR are views along the same horizontal axis from opposite directions; RIGHT and LEFT are views along the perpendicular horizontal axis from opposite directions; TOP looks straight down (+Z); BOTTOM looks straight up from below (-Z). All horizontal projections must show only the appropriate silhouette, cap, or underside; do not show the broad TOP surface in FRONT/REAR/RIGHT/LEFT.

Row 1: the source is a low horizontal rubble/stone slab with scattered cyan crystal-like stone chunks. Keep that identity and scattered arrangement. TOP/BOTTOM may show the corresponding plan. FRONT/RIGHT/LEFT/REAR are low horizontal stone side profiles across the full width with plausible slab depth and small rubble silhouettes; never place the full top map plane upright, never make tall piles or isolated vertical columns.

Row 2: the source is a small upright log-and-timber shelter with a red canopy/roof, spiked log corners, two barrels, and a front doorway. Preserve exactly this shelter identity and its attached props. Make FRONT a straight-on facade with the doorway and canopy edge, REAR the opposite straight-on timber wall under the same roof, RIGHT and LEFT the straight side walls at the same physical height, TOP the roof plan, BOTTOM the plausible ground/support footprint. No diagonal corner views, no two facade planes visible together, no invented windows or extra barrels.

Row 3: the source is a horizontal railway platform edge segment with gray stone deck, bright yellow tactile strip and dark metal/wood support. Keep the same material and source pattern. FRONT/REAR show a low horizontal slab edge; RIGHT/LEFT show low horizontal perpendicular edge profiles, not tall posts or broad upright panels. TOP is the deck plan, BOTTOM the physical underside with supports. Keep the tactile surface on TOP and occluded from below, with consistent slab thickness and footprint.

Maintain coherent proportions and repeated details across each row; draw only inferred unseen surfaces conservatively from the supplied source and current views.

provenance.prompt:
Create a crisp pixel-art atlas on a fully transparent background, exactly SIX COLUMNS by SIX ROWS, no text or borders. Columns in exact order FRONT, TOP, RIGHT, LEFT, BOTTOM, REAR. Rows in exact order faction-larracos-larracos-college-of-magic-entrance; iron-tracks-tunnel-stone-open-doorway; hunting-jungle-vine-covered-ruin-stone-open-doorway; industry-menagerie-soot-stained-brick-open-doorway; faction-battlefield-fortified-camp-gate; early-arenas-gated-stone-bridge. The attached contact sheet has a canonical SOURCE followed by current views in each row; the SOURCE is the authority for that row’s material, ornament, count, and open/closed state. Preserve source identity exactly; never borrow another row’s motifs. True orthographic axis-aligned views only, no isometric or perspective. FRONT/REAR are straight elevations with no visible top; TOP looks straight down and BOTTOM straight up; RIGHT/LEFT are edge-on side elevations. Keep consistent physical proportions across directions. Each cell contains one object, centered, separated with transparent margin; no detached specks or neighboring-cell overlap.

ROW 1 faction-larracos-larracos-college-of-magic-entrance: pale carved stone arch with blue magical inset and paired small statues. TOP must be the full shallow arch, pillar, statue-base footprint seen from directly above, with no frontal arch face; BOTTOM is the matching pale-stone foundation underside, same complete footprint, no generic square panel. Preserve paired statues; do not invent posts or extra objects.

ROW 2 iron-tracks-tunnel-stone-open-doorway: open stone tunnel portal with moss and dark passage. TOP is only the shallow lintel and post-cap surfaces in plan, with dark opening empty; BOTTOM is the matching threshold/foot underside, not a frontal wall with stacked masonry courses. Preserve visible opening and source moss/stone.

ROW 3 hunting-jungle-vine-covered-ruin-stone-open-doorway: open overgrown stone doorway with vines. TOP is a compact orthographic arch/frame footprint with thin vine and stone edge details, not a floor tile; BOTTOM is the matching stone foundation underside. REAR shows the reverse side of the same open through-passage: paired jambs and arch, empty opening, not a sealed masonry wall.

ROW 4 industry-menagerie-soot-stained-brick-open-doorway: open soot-dark brick and stone arch with steel corner braces. TOP is a shallow arch-lintel plan with cap stones above the passage, not an upright frontal arch; BOTTOM is a matching narrow foundation/threshold underside, not the front door face. REAR is the reverse elevation with the same open passage, no brick wall closing it. Keep the source dark red brick and gray stone.

ROW 5 faction-battlefield-fortified-camp-gate: rough timber gate with two posts, beam, hanging green cloth banners and rocks. TOP has the gate beam and two post caps/rocks as an overhead footprint; hanging cloth presents as thin hems, not broad flag faces. BOTTOM has timber post-foot undersides and ground-anchored structure at the same footprint, not a generic full square ground patch. Preserve the source two-post count and green cloth.

ROW 6 early-arenas-gated-stone-bridge: dark timber bridge deck between pale stone posts and railings. FRONT/REAR are bridge-end elevations with the deck edge and paired stone posts, not the overhead walkway tilted upright. RIGHT/LEFT are long low side elevations with horizontal bridge deck and railing spans along X, coherent with the source plan. Keep the same count of stone posts, no additional gates or panels.

provenance.prompt:
Create ONE transparent-background, orthographic pixel-art six-view atlas for the small bugbear timber shelter shown in the attached reference sheet. Match the Pocket Dungeon palette, pixel clusters, dark outline and gold-brown log materials. The source icon is a hybrid/isometric map symbol; use it only for identity. Use the accepted TOP and BOTTOM examples for plan shape and material guidance. Do not copy the source's angled camera.

Exactly 6 columns in this order: FRONT, TOP, RIGHT, LEFT, BOTTOM, REAR. One row, six equal isolated cells. Each cell contains the same whole physical shelter, centered, no labels, no shadows, no cell bleed. Strict axis-aligned orthographic views, camera exactly along world axes, no perspective, no isometric angle, no foreshortening, no diagonal corner view. Keep object world orientation fixed across all six views. FRONT is viewed from -Y, REAR from +Y, RIGHT from +X, LEFT from -X, TOP straight down +Z, BOTTOM straight up from -Z.

The shelter is an upright compact timber/log hut with a red hide canopy roof, four spiked log corner posts, an open dark front entrance and two small wooden barrels at the front. FRONT is a straight-on broad facade; show the entrance centered between the two posts and the same canopy as a shallow roof edge above. REAR is the opposite straight-on broad timber back wall under the roof; no doorway visible from rear. RIGHT and LEFT are straight side elevations: each is a single side wall plane, with the same four-corner-post height and roof edge; do not show the front and side walls together. Keep the vertical post height equal in all four elevations. TOP is the canopy's rectangular plan with the red hide and cross-braces as shown by the accepted TOP example. BOTTOM is the compact ground footprint with post foot ends and closed underside as shown by the accepted BOTTOM example. No invented rooms, extra barrels, windows, props, or people. Transparent background, crisp pixel-art clusters.

provenance.prompt:
Create transparent-background pixel-art atlas with exactly TWO equal square cells side by side, TOP then BOTTOM, of the same narrow alley barricade with barrel and traffic cone in canonical source. The labeled source and accepted FRONT/RIGHT/LEFT/REAR are authoritative for identity, scale, and orientation; ignore incorrect old plan views which show an upright board face. True orthographic projections, straight down for TOP and straight up from below for BOTTOM, no perspective/isometric.

TOP: show the two pale stone post cap footprints at the barricade ends, the crossed/planked wooden barricade as thin low horizontal board strips between them, plus the separate barrel lid and traffic cone tip/circular upper cap projecting in front of the barricade on the same side and at their source locations. Keep the barrel/cone overhang outside the post footprints; do not flatten the full frontal crossed-board face into a large square panel.
BOTTOM: show compact matching post-foot undersides, underside of the thin wooden cross planks/bracing, full barrel base and traffic cone base footprints in correct positions; no upright crossed-board face. Maintain the complete shared XY footprint including barrel/cone offset and shallow barricade depth. Preserve warm brown wood, pale stone, blue-brown barrel, orange-white cone, subtle grass. Center both, transparent margin, no labels, shadow, guide marks or clipping; crisp pixel-art clusters.

provenance.prompt:
Create a transparent-background pixel-art atlas with exactly two side-by-side cells, TOP then BOTTOM, for the same soot-stained brick open doorway shown in the attached reference sheet. The native source alone controls material and identity: reddish soot-stained brick piers, charcoal masonry, pale tan stone arch/lintel, central open black passage. The current source-plus-six sheet supplies the accepted FRONT, RIGHT, LEFT and REAR. The Iron Tracks open doorway plan images are geometry-only examples for shallow doorway footprints; do not copy their materials.

The physical doorway is an upright open arch with shallow wall thickness, broad X width and narrow Y depth. TOP is viewed straight down (+Z); BOTTOM straight up from below (-Z). Both views must be true shallow plan/end-surface projections: broad width across the arch, small depth matching the accepted side elevations. Keep the central passage open as a dark elongated gap; show two side piers at the correct ends and the pale stone lintel/arch cap spanning the opening. Do not draw the full front-facing arch, stacked red brick courses, tall pillars, or a four-corner display panel. No upright door face or bricks visible as vertical front panels.

TOP: pale tan/gray stone upper lintel/crown cap across the doorway, flat brick pier tops at both sides, dark open passage footprint, and subtle charcoal interior rim. BOTTOM: opaque shallow underside of the pale stone lintel and matching pier footing/base cross-sections, with the same dark open passage gap; no top-facing arch face or stacked brick shafts. Preserve the same orientation and footprint in both cells. Center each isolated view, generous transparent margins, no labels or shadows, no cell bleed; crisp Pocket Dungeon pixel-art clusters.

provenance.prompt:
Create a crisp pixel-art atlas on a fully transparent background, exactly SIX COLUMNS by SIX ROWS, no text or borders. Columns in exact order FRONT, TOP, RIGHT, LEFT, BOTTOM, REAR. Rows in exact order faction-larracos-larracos-college-of-magic-entrance; iron-tracks-tunnel-stone-open-doorway; hunting-jungle-vine-covered-ruin-stone-open-doorway; industry-menagerie-soot-stained-brick-open-doorway; faction-battlefield-fortified-camp-gate; early-arenas-gated-stone-bridge. The attached contact sheet has a canonical SOURCE followed by current views in each row; the SOURCE is the authority for that row’s material, ornament, count, and open/closed state. Preserve source identity exactly; never borrow another row’s motifs. True orthographic axis-aligned views only, no isometric or perspective. FRONT/REAR are straight elevations with no visible top; TOP looks straight down and BOTTOM straight up; RIGHT/LEFT are edge-on side elevations. Keep consistent physical proportions across directions. Each cell contains one object, centered, separated with transparent margin; no detached specks or neighboring-cell overlap.

ROW 1 faction-larracos-larracos-college-of-magic-entrance: pale carved stone arch with blue magical inset and paired small statues. TOP must be the full shallow arch, pillar, statue-base footprint seen from directly above, with no frontal arch face; BOTTOM is the matching pale-stone foundation underside, same complete footprint, no generic square panel. Preserve paired statues; do not invent posts or extra objects.

ROW 2 iron-tracks-tunnel-stone-open-doorway: open stone tunnel portal with moss and dark passage. TOP is only the shallow lintel and post-cap surfaces in plan, with dark opening empty; BOTTOM is the matching threshold/foot underside, not a frontal wall with stacked masonry courses. Preserve visible opening and source moss/stone.

ROW 3 hunting-jungle-vine-covered-ruin-stone-open-doorway: open overgrown stone doorway with vines. TOP is a compact orthographic arch/frame footprint with thin vine and stone edge details, not a floor tile; BOTTOM is the matching stone foundation underside. REAR shows the reverse side of the same open through-passage: paired jambs and arch, empty opening, not a sealed masonry wall.

ROW 4 industry-menagerie-soot-stained-brick-open-doorway: open soot-dark brick and stone arch with steel corner braces. TOP is a shallow arch-lintel plan with cap stones above the passage, not an upright frontal arch; BOTTOM is a matching narrow foundation/threshold underside, not the front door face. REAR is the reverse elevation with the same open passage, no brick wall closing it. Keep the source dark red brick and gray stone.

ROW 5 faction-battlefield-fortified-camp-gate: rough timber gate with two posts, beam, hanging green cloth banners and rocks. TOP has the gate beam and two post caps/rocks as an overhead footprint; hanging cloth presents as thin hems, not broad flag faces. BOTTOM has timber post-foot undersides and ground-anchored structure at the same footprint, not a generic full square ground patch. Preserve the source two-post count and green cloth.

ROW 6 early-arenas-gated-stone-bridge: dark timber bridge deck between pale stone posts and railings. FRONT/REAR are bridge-end elevations with the deck edge and paired stone posts, not the overhead walkway tilted upright. RIGHT/LEFT are long low side elevations with horizontal bridge deck and railing spans along X, coherent with the source plan. Keep the same count of stone posts, no additional gates or panels.

provenance.prompt:
Create a transparent-background orthographic pixel-art atlas for the single Iron Stations platform edge segment in the attached reference sheet. Match the source Pocket Dungeon pixel-art palette, outlines, gray concrete, bright yellow tactile tiles, dark steel and wood. The original map icon is a hybrid layout reference, not a camera instruction. Exactly six columns, one row: FRONT, TOP, RIGHT, LEFT, BOTTOM, REAR. One same physical horizontal platform segment in every cell, centered, isolated, generous transparent space, no labels, no perspective, no isometric camera, no tilt, no cell bleed.

The ACCEPTED TOP reference is authoritative for the plan footprint and position of the gray deck, yellow tactile strip and dark rail/support elements. Preserve that arrangement in TOP. The ACCEPTED BOTTOM reference guides the inferred underside only. The platform is a long, low horizontal structure: its long axis is world X; its short/depth axis is world Y; its thickness is a small fraction of either plan dimension. Its total width in FRONT/REAR must match TOP X length; RIGHT/LEFT width must match TOP Y depth. All four horizontal elevations have the same low concrete slab thickness and support height.

FRONT and REAR: strict end elevation across the long X span; show a thin horizontal concrete side edge, dark continuous rail/support profile and timber support blocks. Do not show the broad gray deck plane, yellow raised dots or full map layout on the vertical face. TOP should be visible only as a very thin top rim.

RIGHT and LEFT: strict end-on view along the long rail axis; a compact orthographic profile across the short Y depth, consisting of a gray concrete cap/block, thin dark rail edge and dark/timber underside support, all low and horizontal. Do NOT draw narrow tall yellow-faced posts, vertical columns, or upright tactile panels. The rail/profile must remain horizontal, not upright.

BOTTOM: physical underside looking straight up, opaque coherent support footprint matching the TOP XY outline, with the dark steel/wood backing and support blocks; no yellow tactile bumps visible from below. Keep exact object identity, no additional track pieces or separate objects. Pixel-art clusters crisp and source-faithful.

provenance.prompt:
Create a transparent-background pixel-art atlas with two cells, RIGHT then LEFT, for the short end-on view of the same Iron Stations horizontal platform edge segment. Use the attached native source, accepted TOP plan, and accepted thin FRONT/REAR side-profile candidates for identity and shared Z scale. The earlier end-view candidate is only a material-detail reference; its proportions were wrong.

Each cell MUST be a broad, shallow horizontal cross-section with target silhouette ratio width:height approximately 134:70 (about 1.9:1). Preserve the full TOP plan Y/depth span of about 134 and the exact common vertical thickness of 70 used by the accepted FRONT/REAR profiles. Do not reduce depth or height. Make the profile a solid gray concrete cap across the full horizontal span, a thin dark rail/support course below it, then a shallow dark base with brown timber blocks. Keep all layers aligned along the same horizontal axis.

Camera directions are strictly orthographic from +X for RIGHT and -X for LEFT, no perspective, no isometric view. These should read as short, broad end profiles of a low platform: horizontal width is noticeably longer than height. No tall post, no vertical stack, no upright yellow tactile panel, no raised-dot panel on the side. The yellow tactile surface belongs only on TOP and is hidden in these end views. Preserve source materials and pixel-art cluster style, isolate each complete object and center it with transparent margins, no labels, shadows or neighboring-cell bleed.

provenance.prompt:
Create a crisp pixel-art atlas on a fully transparent background, exactly SIX COLUMNS by SIX ROWS, no text or borders. Columns in exact order FRONT, TOP, RIGHT, LEFT, BOTTOM, REAR. Rows in exact order faction-larracos-larracos-college-of-magic-entrance; iron-tracks-tunnel-stone-open-doorway; hunting-jungle-vine-covered-ruin-stone-open-doorway; industry-menagerie-soot-stained-brick-open-doorway; faction-battlefield-fortified-camp-gate; early-arenas-gated-stone-bridge. The attached contact sheet has a canonical SOURCE followed by current views in each row; the SOURCE is the authority for that row’s material, ornament, count, and open/closed state. Preserve source identity exactly; never borrow another row’s motifs. True orthographic axis-aligned views only, no isometric or perspective. FRONT/REAR are straight elevations with no visible top; TOP looks straight down and BOTTOM straight up; RIGHT/LEFT are edge-on side elevations. Keep consistent physical proportions across directions. Each cell contains one object, centered, separated with transparent margin; no detached specks or neighboring-cell overlap.

ROW 1 faction-larracos-larracos-college-of-magic-entrance: pale carved stone arch with blue magical inset and paired small statues. TOP must be the full shallow arch, pillar, statue-base footprint seen from directly above, with no frontal arch face; BOTTOM is the matching pale-stone foundation underside, same complete footprint, no generic square panel. Preserve paired statues; do not invent posts or extra objects.

ROW 2 iron-tracks-tunnel-stone-open-doorway: open stone tunnel portal with moss and dark passage. TOP is only the shallow lintel and post-cap surfaces in plan, with dark opening empty; BOTTOM is the matching threshold/foot underside, not a frontal wall with stacked masonry courses. Preserve visible opening and source moss/stone.

ROW 3 hunting-jungle-vine-covered-ruin-stone-open-doorway: open overgrown stone doorway with vines. TOP is a compact orthographic arch/frame footprint with thin vine and stone edge details, not a floor tile; BOTTOM is the matching stone foundation underside. REAR shows the reverse side of the same open through-passage: paired jambs and arch, empty opening, not a sealed masonry wall.

ROW 4 industry-menagerie-soot-stained-brick-open-doorway: open soot-dark brick and stone arch with steel corner braces. TOP is a shallow arch-lintel plan with cap stones above the passage, not an upright frontal arch; BOTTOM is a matching narrow foundation/threshold underside, not the front door face. REAR is the reverse elevation with the same open passage, no brick wall closing it. Keep the source dark red brick and gray stone.

ROW 5 faction-battlefield-fortified-camp-gate: rough timber gate with two posts, beam, hanging green cloth banners and rocks. TOP has the gate beam and two post caps/rocks as an overhead footprint; hanging cloth presents as thin hems, not broad flag faces. BOTTOM has timber post-foot undersides and ground-anchored structure at the same footprint, not a generic full square ground patch. Preserve the source two-post count and green cloth.

ROW 6 early-arenas-gated-stone-bridge: dark timber bridge deck between pale stone posts and railings. FRONT/REAR are bridge-end elevations with the deck edge and paired stone posts, not the overhead walkway tilted upright. RIGHT/LEFT are long low side elevations with horizontal bridge deck and railing spans along X, coherent with the source plan. Keep the same count of stone posts, no additional gates or panels.

provenance.prompt: Create transparent-background pixel-art atlas exactly TWO cells side-by-side: FRONT then REAR end elevations of the same unoccupied Parade Horribles float base. The canonical source plus accepted TOP/RIGHT/LEFT/BOTTOM views define identity and dimensions. The deck is horizontal in XY, long axis runs away along Y. FRONT and REAR cameras look horizontally along that Y axis; show only the low, thin vertical deck edge and visible wheel/chassis assembly underneath at the near end, with gold corner hardware and the source red-gold crest on the vertical skirt if that face is visible. Keep the whole horizontal top deck foreshortened to a narrow edge; no broad square top plane turned upright, no overhead projection, no perspective. Both ends must share the same physical low deck height and wheel placement, opposite faces of the same float. Preserve wood/tan deck, dark tires, gold trim, red crest identity. Center each end profile, transparent margins, no labels/shadow/stray fragments/clipping. Pixel-art clusters.

provenance.prompt:
Create a transparent-background pixel-art atlas with exactly TWO equal square cells side-by-side, REAR then BOTTOM, for the UP-oriented short asphalt stair module shown in the canonical source. The labeled reference contact contains the native source and accepted FRONT/TOP/RIGHT/LEFT. Source controls identity and stair direction; accepted TOP/side views fix footprint and tread run. Draw exact orthographic principal projections, no isometric or perspective.

Cell 1 REAR: show the opaque reverse support face at the far end of this same stair flight, a closed dark charcoal/asphalt-backed sloped support with the correct high/low end for the up stair orientation. It must not show the forward-visible tread pattern, and must not depict the opposite up/down state. Retain the source dark asphalt and light side curb materials.
Cell 2 BOTTOM: camera directly below looking up. Show a full-depth underside plane matching the accepted TOP footprint length and side profiles, with plausible plain dark asphalt/stone substrate and side-curb underside along the footprint. Do NOT show any upward tread surfaces, colored lane markings or front-facing stairs. Match the existing TOP XY extent, not half-depth.

Keep both projections centered, their shared world-axis orientation consistent, transparent margins, no guide marks, no labels, no shadows, no clipping, crisp clustered pixel art.
provenance.notes: Root-scoped-accepted full-depth underside. Tread faces remain occluded; no content outside source-supported stair footprint. Pending fresh whole-set review after rear repair.

provenance.prompt:
Generate exactly TWO transparent-background orthographic REAR elevations in a two-cell atlas: UP stairs first, DOWN stairs second. Keep each object’s own source identity and current accepted FRONT/TOP/RIGHT/LEFT/BOTTOM. The accepted FRONT silhouette defines total proportions: normalized bounds about 210px wide by 178px high. Your v1/v2 attempts were only about 210x120 after normalization; this is too short. Draw the REAR with the same full-height silhouette as FRONT, using a taller opaque support/back panel and full-height paired corner posts. This is a geometry generation; do not stretch the old artwork or widen the object.

Camera is straight behind the stair flight, horizontal and orthographic. From this viewpoint, the forward treads are occluded. The back view is a closed, broad dark asphalt/steel rectangle about 210px wide by 178px high, bottom aligned at y=248, framed by two gray steel corner posts that both reach the same top height. The landing appears only as a thin narrow horizontal top edge. There must be no receding wedge and no parallel tread pattern. Preserve the rail caps and source hardware at the top/outer posts. For the DOWN source, preserve its own small source-specific red side sliver if it is visible from rear; do not transfer it to UP. Crisp pixel-art clusters, transparent background, no labels, no shadows, stray guides, or clipping.

provenance.prompt:
Create a transparent-background pixel-art atlas for the exact wooden trophy shelf in the attached labeled source+accepted-view contact. It must contain exactly TWO square orthographic views: TOP, then REAR. Preserve the canonical object's warm wood, shelf dimensions, source item locations, and exactly THREE objects on the upper shelf: one hanging green plant, one gold cup/trophy, one framed photograph. The tiny extra gold object sits on the LOWER shelf in the source; in both requested views it is hidden behind the shelf board and must not appear.

TOP camera: directly above (+Z), true orthographic. The photo frame is upright/tilted and standing on the shelf, not laid flat. Show only its narrow top edge and small support/stand footprint. Do not show any photo image or rectangular frontal picture face. Show the plant's leaf canopy footprint and the open circular rim of one gold cup. Keep a thin wooden upper-shelf board beneath these footprints. Do not add any extra object.

REAR camera: directly behind (-Y), true orthographic. Show the plain wood back of the frame and rear of the SAME plant and cup, at the same positions and proportions as the accepted elevations. The lower-shelf gold ornament is occluded behind the shelf board and must not appear. No frontal picture image.

Preserve source count and identity exactly. Center each isolated object on a transparent canvas with full shelf width, no crop, no added labels, grid, shadow, detached guide marks, extra gold ornament, or perspective. Crisp pixel-art clusters.

provenance.prompt:
Generate ONE transparent-background, crisp pixel-art orthographic REAR view of the exact Surface Entry Trophy Shelf in the attached contact. The contact includes canonical source, current accepted principal views and an earlier REAR silhouette reference. Source identity and accepted FRONT determine the full object dimensions. This object is a tall freestanding three-row bookcase, not a short wall shelf. The REAR sprite must occupy a full square-like footprint: about 176 px wide by 176 px high at 256x256, bottom aligned to y=248. Do not shorten it or anisotropically stretch it.

Camera is straight-on from directly behind (-Y), orthographic, level. Preserve the entire tall bookcase: two full-height side posts from top to floor, a closed continuous warm-brown wooden backboard spanning the full height behind the three source shelf rows, and subtle horizontal shelf/back seams at the corresponding three-row heights. The base and top rails stay at the same Z positions as FRONT. Keep full height from the highest source plant/photo/cup to the bottom corner feet; common X width matches accepted FRONT (176 px native alpha bounds), overall alpha extent approximately 176x176.

At the top edge, retain exactly these three top-shelf projections in source order and scale: drooping green plant at left, ONE gold cup near center, and the back of the framed photograph near right. The lower-shelf small gold ornament is occluded and must be absent. Do not show the photo face. Do not remove or shrink the three-row bookcase body. No open cubby/rack/single shelf, no full frontal image, no extra ornament, no perspective, shadows, labels, detached guides, or clipping. Use the same wood tone, gold corner hardware, plant green, and gold cup as the supplied source/elevations.
